verdicts.summary: The module queue has no pruning and no mount-time flush. Prompts that the desktop has already abandoned stay in the queue and show as stacked modal 'Expired' dialogs after sign-in.
verdicts.scenario: 1) App starts on /welcome, /pair, /connect, the guest page or an unauthenticated route. An enabled SSH environment E has no cached password (e.g. after restart). 2) E's connect calls ensureSshEnvironment (platform.ts:198, 276); the desktop sends prompt P1 (3-minute expiry, DesktopSshPasswordPrompts.ts:18, 320-322). startSshPasswordPromptQueue appends it (SshPasswordPromptDialog.tsx:51-53). No dialog is rendered on these routes: SshPasswordPromptDialog is only at __root.tsx:239, after the early returns at :165-212. 3) After 3 minutes the desktop times out and its cleanup drops P1 silently (DesktopSshPasswordPrompts.ts:378-380). The renderer never learns and keeps P1. 4) The supervisor retries with backoff (supervisor.ts:127-129), E prompts again, and P2 is appended with no dedupe or bound. 5) The user signs in 15 minutes later. The dialog opens on P1 showing 'Expired' (SshPasswordPromptDialog.tsx:104-106, 211-212). Each stale entry needs a Dismiss click, and a live prompt queued behind them is hidden while its own 3-minute window keeps running.
verdicts.consequence: A stack of modal 'Expired' dialogs blocks the shell after sign-in, one per failed password attempt made while no dialog was mounted. The count grows with time spent before sign-in. A live prompt queued behind stale ones is hidden until each is dismissed. Before this commit these prompts were dropped at the listener, so the stack is new.
verdicts.missing: Not checked: whether the desktop re-raises prompts on its own without a new connect attempt, and whether a supervisor reconnect restarts the SSH command after a failure.

verdicts.summary: Escape is consumed exactly as before on /pull-requests. A page-level capture listener and any scope that calls preventDefault both stop the observer from acting. The only global scopes are navigation back/forward, and both call preventDefault. Not checked: the __TSR_index !== 0 equivalence with useCanGoBack, because the TanStack source is not in the checkout.
verdicts.scenario: Escape pressed on /pull-requests while the PR page's own document-capture Escape listener is active. That listener calls preventDefault and cancels the close sweep, so the observer's consumed flag is true and it returns without navigating. The same holds for any global scope that handles Escape, since navigation back/forward call preventDefault.

verdicts.summary: The probe result replaces the fallback only when the probe returns a non-empty remote-capable list. A rejection or empty result keeps the vscode fallback, as the old code did. The atom is keepAlive, so there is one probe per page.
verdicts.scenario: The probe rejects, or resolves with an empty or non-remote-capable list. The rejection handler is a no-op and the empty list is skipped, so the atom keeps REMOTE_FALLBACK_EDITORS. The first read is the only trigger for the probe, and keepAlive prevents re-probing.

verdicts.summary: Finding 1 raises the same question (do the shell subscriptions start connections before auth?). I confirmed the answer is yes, and its consequence is written up as the added hazard A below rather than repeated here. The announcer's memory-while-detached behaviour was checked and is not a regression: on remount, the old code also seeded silently.

Hazard A (answers finding 1): the early subscription starts connection supervisors before sign-in on /pair, /connect, /connect-agent, the guest page and unauthenticated routes. Those routes did not render AppSidebarLayout before this commit.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Launch the desktop on /pair or an unauthenticated route. Before this commit, AppSidebarLayout (__root.tsx:196, 216) was not rendered there, so no shell atoms were mounted. /welcome already rendered it (:196), so /welcome is not newly affected. 2) startAppServices subscribes quietThreadShellsAtom and threadShellsAtom (appInit.tsx:134-135). 3) Mounting walks to environmentThreadsAtom for every enabled environment (threadShell.ts:376-383), then to environmentShell.stateAtom (shell.ts:617-621), then to followStream (registry.ts:431-451). acquireSupervisor then creates a supervisor with initiallyDesired = entry.enabled (registry.ts:362) and forkIn(scope) (registry.ts:382). 4) Every enabled environment starts connecting before sign-in. For SSH targets, each attempt calls ensureSshEnvironment (platform.ts:198, 276), which raises a desktop password prompt that the hidden queue holds (note 0). The desktop focuses the window each time (DesktopSshPasswordPrompts.ts:457).
verdicts.consequence: Connection and SSH auth work runs on pairing and sign-in pages that never ran it before. The desktop window is focused every ~3 minutes for prompts the user cannot see on those pages.
verdicts.missing: Not checked: whether the pairing page or the unauthenticated primary environment already starts these supervisors through another path. I did not read the connection driver's behaviour when an unauthenticated environment connects.

verdicts.summary: Hazard B: the visit migration marks a thread as migrated before the server acknowledges the visit. A failed visit is never retried in this page life. The early mount runs this on more routes.
verdicts.scenario: A cached or non-live snapshot exposes a thread with lastVisitedAt and a local visit newer than the server's value. migratedThreadKeys.add runs before runAtomCommand (:21-22, :29-34). runAtomCommand is called with reportFailure:false, and failures are returned as results, not thrown or warned (runtime.ts:455-466). If the visit fails (for example, the server is unreachable; I did not read the command's failure path), the key stays marked and no retry happens until reload.
verdicts.consequence: A local visit timestamp never reaches the server during this page life. It is silently lost, and no warning is logged.
verdicts.missing: The visit command's behaviour when the environment is not live: whether it fails or waits (runtime.ts only shows result reporting).
